title: Incremental chunked embedding harvester with resumable uploads and opaque idempotency
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Large customers need to stream or bulk-upload millions of documents for embedding/reranking. Current ingest is optimized for small-batch synchronous calls and a separate async importer, but customers face: 1) high retry complexity when uploads fail mid-stream, 2) duplicate vectors from client retries, 3) unpredictable memory spikes when clients send large batches, and 4) wide variability in latency from ingest to index availability.

Proposed solution: Implement an incremental, chunked ingestion API and backend pipeline that provides resumable uploads, opaque idempotency handles, and an async job model. Key pieces:
- Client uploads are split into sequence-numbered chunks with a single client-provided idempotency_key and optional per-chunk checksum.
- Server returns a resumable handle (server-signed) after initial chunk, allowing clients to resume by chunk index rather than re-sending entire batches.
- Worker-side fanout: chunks are sharded by a deterministic customer-aware routing key and processed by a pool of embed workers that support exactly-once commit semantics using week-long checkpoint leases.
- Deduplication by canonicalized document hash + idempotency_key to prevent duplicates from concurrent retry windows.
- Async job API: POST /v1/embeds/async with manifest or direct streaming. Server returns job_id; job state transitions are reported via webhook or polled APIs. For very large uploads clients may provide an S3 manifest to reduce intermediary memory usage.
- Backpressure and flow control: server will advertise a per-client concurrency window and return 429 + Retry-After when workers are saturated; clients may use a recommended dynamic chunk size (default 2k tokens / chunk) and adapt based on 95th percentile processing time.
- Observability: ingest timeline traces (upload -> encode -> index commit), per-job token counts, dedupe counts, and a consumer-facing dashboard showing ETA to index availability.

Goals: reduce end-to-end availability latency for large bulk jobs, ensure idempotent semantics for retries, provide resume capability to avoid restarting multi-hour uploads, and keep memory/cost bounded on server side.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/embeds/async supports chunked uploads and returns a server-signed resumable_handle and job_id
Semantics: Replaying the same chunk sequence under the same idempotency_key must not create duplicate vectors (within a 14-day dedupe window)
Resume: A client can resume an interrupted upload at chunk N using resumable_handle without re-uploading chunks 0..N-1
Latency: For a 1M-document job split into 10k-chunk batches, 95% of jobs reach index availability within 120 seconds of final chunk commit under normal cluster load
Backpressure: Server exposes per-client concurrency window and returns 429 with Retry-After when window exhausted
Monitoring: New ingest dashboard shows job lifecycle, per-chunk processing latency percentiles, and dedupe rate; alerts fire if median processing time > 30s for 5m
Data correctness: Deduplication verified by canonical hash; integration test harness demonstrates no duplicates across 5 concurrent client retry scenarios
Cost safety: Server memory footprint per active job stays < 1 GB for jobs up to 5M documents using S3 manifest flow
notes: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on resumable_handle design and trade-offs between server-signed handles and opaque token-only resume. Decided on server-signed handle to avoid unbounded server state.
2026-02-18: Prototype: simple chunked POST implemented; proved resume by chunk index against local worker pool. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1943
2026-02-25: Decision: dedupe keys will be canonicalized SHA256 of normalized text + client id; TTL=14 days. Reason: content-hash gives robust dedupe across chunk reordering and partial retries.

2026-03-02: Performance bench: single standard embed worker can process ~2.4k 512-token documents/s (fp16 quant path). Using sharded workers, we project 100k docs/s cluster throughput for typical Dedicated pools.

2026-03-05: UX note: added 'manifest' mode where clients upload a newline-delimited manifest (s3://) and server pulls files asynchronously to avoid memory spikes. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Chunked+Embeddings+Manifest+Flow
2026-03-09: Security: KMS review not required for handle signing; using service key rotation. Security asked that webhook payloads are HMAC-signed — implemented in webhook spec (see doc).
2026-03-12: Integration tests added in CI that simulate flaky networks and confirm resume and dedupe behaviour. Test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings/pull/827

2026-03-14: Current work: implementing server-side checkpoint lease store and extending worker commit protocol to support commit-idempotency and tombstone records. Estimated 2 more sprints for full rollout to hosted region us-west2.
implementation_plan: API: Add /v1/embeds/async with chunked upload and resumable_handle generation (server-signed JWT-like token)
Storage: Implement per-job checkpoint metadata in Dynamo/Etcd with lease TTL and graceful reclaim
Workers: Update embed workers to accept chunked payloads, compute canonical hash, and write vector commit with dedupe-protection
Backpressure: Implement concurrency window service that reports allowed inflight chunks per customer and integrates with 429 behavior
Observability: Instrument traces (OpenTelemetry), job-level metrics, and expose dashboard panel; hook alerts for processing latency regression
Client SDKs: Add resumable upload helpers in Python/Node SDKs with default chunk sizing and retry backoff
QA: Add fuzz+replay CI tests, run soak across staging cluster with synthetic 10M doc job
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Lease store hotkeys for very large customers could cause contention — Mitigation: shard lease space by customer and job hash, and add exponential backoff and jitter in reclaim path
Risk: Duplicate vectors due to race window when worker commit fails after vector write — Mitigation: write idempotency tombstone before final index commit and use conditional-upsert on commit path
Risk: Clients misuse resumable_handle to resume with different idempotency_key — Mitigation: resumable_handle encodes customer_id and original idempotency_key fingerprint; server validates on resume
Risk: Cost regression from holding large numbers of in-flight chunks — Mitigation: manifest/S3 mode for bulk ingestion and default chunk size conservative; add server-side eviction policy
